name: Applications & Interfaces
oneLiner: Where people meet AI: chat assistants, copilots inside existing tools, and specialised apps.

analogy.text: A shopfront: customers see the counter and the product, not the warehouse and supply chain behind it.
analogy.breaks: A shop sells the same product every time. AI apps produce different output each time, so interfaces must handle uncertainty, errors and human review.

givesAbove: Value to people, plus usage and feedback that flow back down the stack.
needsBelow: Agents or orchestrated model calls from the layers below.

walkthrough.title: Monday starts in a chat app
walkthrough.text: Sam asks a chat assistant to plan the week. It searches the web and books a table using a browser agent.

walkthrough.title: Hands busy, so Sam talks
walkthrough.text: While cooking, Sam asks out loud and shows the phone camera the fridge. Speech and images go in; a spoken reply comes back.

walkthrough.title: AI hidden inside an app
walkthrough.text: At work, the expenses app has a “summarise receipts” button. Behind it, the app's server calls a model with Sam's own data.

walkthrough.title: A copilot in the editor
walkthrough.text: In the code editor, a copilot suggests changes and, in agent mode, fixes a bug while Sam reviews the diff.
